stories.title: Nvidia allegedly engineered scarcity by funding AI startups to buy its GPUs
stories.blurb: Explosive allegation: Nvidia secretly funded AI startups specifically so they'd turn around and buy its own GPUs, artificially inflating demand and justifying sky-high prices. If true, this is a stunning vertical squeeze on the entire AI supply chain. Directly relevant to anyone budgeting for GPU compute.

stories.title: Jonathan Blow – If AI solved coding, why is my software still the same? [video]
stories.blurb: Jonathan Blow delivers a characteristically sharp critique: if AI coding tools are as transformative as claimed, why hasn't software quality measurably improved? Essential viewing for anyone using Claude Code or Copilot daily — it sharpens the question of what we're actually getting from these tools.

stories.title: Ggml v1.0.0
stories.blurb: The foundational tensor library powering llama.cpp, Whisper, and countless local AI tools finally hits 1.0. This is a milestone for the entire local-inference ecosystem — a stable ABI and API means downstream projects can stop chasing a moving target.

stories.title: Terminal borders that don't cost a cell
stories.blurb: A clever deep dive into rendering terminal UI borders using Unicode half-block and braille characters so they don't consume an extra grid cell. If you build TUIs or use ratatui/Ink, this technique immediately buys back precious screen real estate.

stories.title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
stories.blurb: An empirical deep dive into LeCun's JEPA architecture after hundreds of ablation experiments — this is the kind of painstaking, non-hype AI research that rarely surfaces. The findings on where JEPA world models succeed and break down are genuinely illuminating for anyone thinking beyond autoregressive LLMs.

stories.title: Tech Companies Are Trying to Shift the Concept of Privacy (Again)
stories.blurb: The EFF flags the latest industry push to redefine privacy away from individual rights toward vague "privacy-safe" data practices that still allow broad data harvesting. If you care about the Apple privacy ecosystem and digital rights, this is exactly the narrative battle worth watching.

stories.title: The Claude Delusion
stories.blurb: A critical essay examining the gap between what Claude (and LLMs generally) appear to understand versus what they actually do — with concrete failure examples. Required reading for Claude Code users who need a clear-eyed view of where to trust and where to verify.

stories.title: Found: A protein that drives ageing without unleashing inflammation
stories.blurb: Researchers identified a protein that accelerates cellular aging through a separate pathway from inflammaging — potentially opening a new therapeutic target. The decoupling of aging from inflammation is a surprising and significant finding in longevity biology.

stories.title: Monkey Island: all 13 versions side by side
stories.blurb: A stunning side-by-side comparison of every Monkey Island release across 30+ years of ports and remasters — scroll-synced so you can see pixel art, CD-ROM art, and modern remasters aligned frame by frame. A must-bookmark for anyone who loves game visual history.

stories.title: FM-1 Workbench
stories.blurb: An in-browser FM synthesizer workbench that exposes the full operator graph for designing sounds — no install required. For anyone interested in synthesis or audio programming, it's a surprisingly deep tool that makes the famously opaque FM paradigm approachable.

stories.title: Introducing Claude Meetings
stories.blurb: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings — a native meeting intelligence feature integrated directly into Claude. For anyone already in the Claude ecosystem using Claude Code, this extends the assistant into the meeting layer, potentially replacing standalone transcription tools.

stories.title: microsoft/Procexp-Mac: Process Explorer for MacOS
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: microsoft, Mac, desktop, subject:cs.PF
stories.blurb: Microsoft open-sourced a native macOS port of Sysinternals Process Explorer, built in Swift/SwiftUI with AppKit. It delivers a live process tree, module/handle inspection, code-signing details, and Metal-backed performance graphs — filling a long-standing gap in macOS system tooling.

stories.title: how the Model Context Protocol works
stories.blurb: A visual, step-by-step walkthrough of every MCP message on the wire — transports, auth, tools, sampling, tasks, and tool search. If you're building or consuming MCP servers with Claude Code or other agents, this is the clearest technical reference available.

stories.title: AWS gives developers a free local stand-in for its cloud, built from scratch by AI agents – GeekWire
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: amazon, GenAI, AI.agent, code
stories.blurb: AWS released a free local emulator for its cloud services, reportedly built entirely by AI agents — letting developers test against realistic AWS behavior without network calls or costs. The meta-story (AI agents writing the emulator) is as interesting as the tool itself.

stories.title: Badgeify — Add Any App to Your Mac Menu Bar
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: macos, software, menubar, totry
stories.blurb: Badgeify lets you pin any macOS app as a persistent menu bar icon with live badge counts — handy for surfacing notification counts from apps that don't natively support the menu bar. A simple quality-of-life addition for Mac power users.

stories.title: Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs · Unemployment Labs
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: GenAI, china, regulation, hardware
stories.blurb: Researchers used checkpoint forensics to find signatures in Chinese frontier AI model weights consistent with training on Blackwell GPUs — hardware that is export-controlled. If the methodology holds up, this is a significant finding at the intersection of AI and geopolitics.

stories.title: rVPN · Encrypted stealth VPN over WebSocket/TLS
stories.blurb: rVPN is an open-source stealth VPN that tunnels traffic over WebSocket/TLS, making it indistinguishable from ordinary HTTPS — meaning it works in environments that block conventional VPN protocols. A useful tool to know about for privacy-conscious devs working from restrictive networks.

stories.title: 'Ahead of his time': AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: articles, Guardian, news, subject:cs.AI, subject:cs.CL, claude, science, kurt_godel, mathematics, history, inspiration, year:2026
stories.blurb: Claude was used to analyze Kurt Gödel's handwritten notebooks and discovered he was a single step away from proving the independence of the axiom of choice — decades before it was formally established. A remarkable demonstration of AI as a research partner on genuinely hard intellectual problems.

stories.title: janestreet/agent_skills: Agent skills
stories.blurb: Jane Street open-sourced a collection of agent skill primitives, including a Socratic tutor that teaches any topic using a diagnostic, skill-mapped curriculum with spaced review. Directly useful for anyone building LLM-powered learning or tutoring applications.

stories.title: Vibes Don't Maintain | bacon roll
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: engineering, ai, work
stories.blurb: A sharp engineering post arguing that AI-assisted "vibe coding" produces code that feels fast to write but accumulates hidden maintenance debt that eventually crushes velocity. A timely counterpoint to the hype, especially relevant to developers relying on Claude Code for production codebases.
